description: You are flying to Europe in three days and you are concerned about device theft and border inspections. You want your Mac to lock itself quickly and be harder to access if it leaves your hands. Open System Settings and make these five changes: (1) enable Dark appearance globally — a darker screen is less readable to shoulder-surfers in airports, (2) set the screen saver to start after no more than 2 minutes of inactivity (find this in Screen Saver settings), (3) require a password immediately when the screen saver begins or the display turns off — this is in the Lock Screen pane, (4) set the password delay to 0 seconds (no grace period — password required immediately on wake), and (5) set the top-left hot corner to Lock Screen in Desktop & Dock settings, so you can lock the Mac instantly with one mouse flick. All five changes must persist — the verifier reads NSGlobalDomain, com.apple.screensaver, and com.apple.dock.

metadata.scenario: personal security — hardening Mac privacy settings before international travel
